questionText: Amar walks a certain distance from A to B and rides back from B to A taking a total time of 37 minutes. He could walk both ways A to B and B to A in 55 minutes. How long will it take Amar to ride both ways?
hints: Walking both ways takes 55 min, so walking ONE way takes half of that. Then ride one way = 37 − walk one way.
Walk one way + ride one way = 37 min. Walk one way = 55 ÷ 2.

questionText: A seagull travelled 16500 miles from Finland to Australia. It travelled at a rate of 125 miles per day. In how many days did the seagull reach Australia?
hints: Time = Distance ÷ Speed. Try dividing 16500 by 125 — or divide both by 25 first to make it easier.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

questionText: A motorcycle is moving at the rate of 30 m/s. Its speed in km/hr is:
hints: To change m/s into km/h multiply by 18 ÷ 5 (or by 3.6).

stepByStep.text: 1 km is 1000 m and 1 hour is 3600 seconds. So to change m/s into km/hr, multiply by 3600 and divide by 1000, which is the same as multiplying by 18/5.

questionText: A train 200 m long passes a pole in 9 seconds. The speed of the train in km/hr is:
hints: Passing a pole means covering its own length (200 m). Find the speed in m/s, then change to km/h (× 18/5).
Speed = Distance ÷ Time. m/s → km/h: × 18/5.

questionText: Walking at a speed of 6 km/hr, what distance would he cover in 3 minutes?
hints: How many metres does he walk in 1 hour? Then in 1 minute?
6 km/h = 6000 m in 60 minutes = 100 m per minute.

questionText: In what time will a train 100 m long running at a speed of 36 km/hr pass a man standing by the rails?
hints: Change 36 km/h to m/s (× 5/18). The train must travel its own length to pass the man.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed. km/h → m/s: × 5/18.

questionText: A man walks 900 metres in 18 minutes. How much distance would he cover in an hour?
hints: Find how far he walks in 1 minute. An hour has 60 minutes. Then change metres to km.
Unitary method: distance in 1 minute × 60. 1000 m = 1 km.

questionText: At a speed of 72 km/hr a car will cover a distance of 18 km in how much time?
hints: Time = Distance ÷ Speed. 18 ÷ 72 is a fraction of an hour. Change that into minutes.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed. 1 hour = 60 minutes.

questionText: An ant moves 15 feet per minute. How many feet does it travel in 24 minutes and 40 seconds?
hints: Split the time: 24 minutes and 40 seconds. In 40 seconds the ant covers 2/3 of a minute's distance.
Distance = speed × time.

questionText: An insect flies at the rate of 10 m/sec. What is its speed in km/hr?
hints: To change m/s into km/h multiply by 18 ÷ 5 (or 3.6).

stepByStep.text: (In 1 hour = 3600 seconds, it flies 36,000 m = 36 km ✓)

questionText: An aeroplane departs from Mumbai at 6:20 p.m. and reaches Dubai at 8:50 p.m. If the speed of the aeroplane is 212.5 m/s, find the distance between Mumbai and Dubai.
hints: Find the flying time and change it to seconds, because the speed is in metres per second. Then change metres into km.
Distance = speed × time. 1000 m = 1 km.

questionText: A train 120 metres long running with a speed of 36 km/hr will pass a pole in ____ seconds.
hints: Change 36 km/h to m/s (× 5/18). Passing a pole means covering its own length.
Time = Length ÷ Speed. km/h → m/s: × 5/18.

questionText: A car travels 600 metres in 25 sec. How much distance will the car cover in 1 hour?
hints: Find the speed in metres per second. In 1 hour there are 3600 seconds. Then change metres to km.
Distance = speed × time. 1000 m = 1 km.

stepByStep.text: One hour has 3600 seconds, so in 1 hour the car covers 24 × 3600 = 86400 metres.
86.4 km is not one of the choices given, so the answer is "None of these".

questionText: Shraddha runs five rounds around a 400 m track in her school. For each round she runs the first 100 metres at 4 m/s and the remaining 300 m at 5 m/s. How much time did Shraddha take to complete the five rounds?
hints: Find the time for ONE round in two parts (time = distance ÷ speed). Add them, then multiply by 5 and change seconds into minutes.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

stepByStep.text: First 100 m: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 s. Remaining 300 m: 300 ÷ 5 = 60 s.
One round takes 25 + 60 = 85 s, so five rounds take 85 × 5 = 425 s.
425 s is 7 minutes 5 seconds, because 7 × 60 = 420 and 5 seconds are left.
7 minutes 5 seconds is not one of the choices given, so the answer is "none of these".

questionText: Nirav covers a distance of 680 km in 8 hours from A to B. On his return journey from B to A, he reduced his speed by 17 km/hr. In how much time will he be back to A from B?
hints: Find his speed from A to B first (Distance ÷ Time). Subtract 17 for the return, then find the time. The answer needs to be in MINUTES.
Speed = Distance ÷ Time and Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

questionText: A train departs from London at 6:45 pm and reaches Paris at 9:15 pm on the same day. If the speed of the train is 32.5 m/s, find the distance between London and Paris.
hints: First find how long the journey takes. Then change that time into seconds, because the speed is in metres per second.
Distance = Speed × Time. (1000 m = 1 km)

stepByStep.text: 6:45 pm to 9:15 pm = 2 hours 30 minutes = 9000 seconds.

questionText: A train crosses a pole in 28 seconds, running at a speed of 108 km/hr. Find the length of the train.
hints: Change the speed from km/h to m/s first. Crossing a pole means the train covers exactly its own length.
km/h → m/s: multiply by 5/18. Length = Speed × Time.

questionText: To cover a distance of 432 km travelling at a speed of 24 m/s, how much time will be required?
hints: The distance is in km but the speed is in m/s. Make the units match — change 24 m/s to km/h.
m/s → km/h: multiply by 18/5. Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

stepByStep.text: Make the units match. 24 m/s in km/h is 24 × 18 ÷ 5 = 86.4 km/h.
5 hours is not one of the choices given, so the answer is "None of these".
